changeSet.author: nexus-cbo4a
changeSet.comment: nexus_test.analyze_table(regclass): plpgsql wrapper running EXECUTE format('ANALYZE %s', target) for PgContainerHelper#analyzeTable. plpgsql because ANALYZE is a utility statement SQL-language bodies reject; regclass so PostgreSQL resolves the identity and there is no string to validate; SECURITY INVOKER so the caller's own privilege authorizes the ANALYZE.

changeSet.author: nexus-cbo4a
changeSet.comment: nexus_test.add_fk_not_valid(regclass, text, text, regclass, text, text): plpgsql wrapper for ALTER TABLE .. ADD CONSTRAINT .. FOREIGN KEY (tenant_id, p_column) REFERENCES .. (tenant_id, p_ref_column) p_extra NOT VALID -- a Postgres-only ALTER TABLE extension with no jOOQ typed-DSL form (batch 10 review fold-in). p_table/p_ref are regclass so PostgreSQL resolves each table identity with no string to validate; p_name/p_column/p_ref_column are %I-quoted identifiers; p_extra is the caller-supplied ON UPDATE/ON DELETE clause fragment (e.g. 'ON DELETE RESTRICT'), inserted via %s since it is not a single identifier -- always a fixed literal from Java call sites, never end-user input. Every caller's composite FK is (tenant_id, X) -> (tenant_id, Y), so tenant_id is hardcoded as the first column on both sides rather than adding two more parameters no call site would vary. SECURITY INVOKER so the caller's own (superuser, in every test) privilege authorizes the ALTER TABLE.
changeSet.rollback: DROP FUNCTION IF EXISTS nexus_test.add_fk_not_valid(regclass, text, text, regclass, text, text)

changeSet.author: nexus-3wh8d.16
changeSet.comment: RDR-225 (nexus-3wh8d.16) row-level-security defect injectors for the isolation-check tests, in the same shape as test-objects-5's set_force_rls: plpgsql wrappers over DDL with no jOOQ typed-DSL form (ALTER TABLE .. ENABLE/DISABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY, DROP/ALTER/CREATE POLICY). Every table is a regclass so PostgreSQL resolves the identity with no string to validate; every policy name is %I-quoted. reset_tenant_policy puts the canonical tenant_isolation policy (tenant_id = current_setting('nexus.tenant', true), USING and WITH CHECK) back on a relation, which is how a test repairs a parent whose policy it dropped or widened. SECURITY INVOKER: the caller's own (table-owner) privilege authorizes the DDL.

changeSet.author: nexus-3wh8d.13
changeSet.comment: RDR-225: nexus_test.add_fk_not_valid_composite3 re-adds a (tenant_id, collection, chash) foreign key; once both the referencing and the referenced table carry embedding_model (the partitioned chunks and the tables that reference it, after vectors-030-1) the key is the FOUR-column one, and a three-column key onto chunks has no unique key to rest on. The function therefore appends embedding_model to both column lists when both tables have the column, and is otherwise unchanged, so the pre-walk callers and the same signature keep working. SECURITY INVOKER.

changeSet.author: nexus-cbo4a
changeSet.comment: nexus_test.grant_execute_on_function(text, text): plpgsql wrapper for GRANT EXECUTE ON FUNCTION p_signature TO p_role (nexus-cbo4a batch 11). GRANT EXECUTE ON FUNCTION has no jOOQ typed-DSL form -- jOOQ's GRANT DSL (DSLContext#grant/ GrantOnStep#on) targets tables (Table<?>/Name/String identifiers), not a function's parenthesized argument-type signature, which is what Postgres's GRANT ... ON FUNCTION syntax actually requires after the function name. p_signature is the caller-supplied function-name-plus-arg-types fragment (e.g. "nexus.gc_quarantine_orphans(int, text, text, text, text, int)"), inserted via %s since it is not a single identifier -- always a fixed literal from Java call sites, never end-user input, exactly the same shape add_fk_not_valid_composite3's p_extra clause already uses; p_role is %I-quoted. SECURITY INVOKER so the caller's own (superuser, in every test) privilege authorizes the GRANT. This pattern recurs raw across ~15 other test files today (out of nexus-cbo4a batch 11's scope) -- a follow-up batch can rewire them onto this same function.

changeSet.author: nexus-ft04v.4
changeSet.comment: nexus_test.insert_chunk_bare_vector(text, text, bytea, int): plpgsql wrapper inserting one nexus.chunks row with a BARE (unqualified) ::vector cast built entirely server-side -- for tests that seed vector data at a migration point BEFORE search-path-001-relocate-vector-extensions.xml has relocated the pgvector extension into the nexus schema (Hygiene002CollectionAttributesWalkTest.walkPopulatesEveryBranchAcrossTwoTenants...: hygiene-002-1 runs before search-path-001 in the changelog, so a jOOQ-generated INSERT -- whose compiled binding casts to the schema-qualified "nexus.vector" fixed at codegen time against a FULLY relocated cluster -- fails with "type nexus.vector does not exist" at that point; a bare, unqualified ::vector cast resolves via whatever the connecting role's search_path finds at EXECUTION time, exactly like Hygiene001NotNullMigrationRlsTest's own seedLegacyChunkAndManifest raw-SQL precedent, generalised into a reusable function so no Java caller needs its own raw SQL string). The bare cast is deliberately the ONLY form valid against BOTH substrates this function's callers use: a pre-walk dedicated container (extension still in public, in every role's default search_path) and the shared, fully-migrated cluster (extension relocated to nexus, which search-path-002 adds to the migrating role's own search_path) -- a schema-qualified cast picks one and breaks the other. p_dim selects which embedding_<dim> column receives the value via %I-quoted dynamic column name; the "[0.1,0.1,...]" literal of length p_dim is built via generate_series/string_agg, never string-concatenated in Java. SECURITY INVOKER so the caller's own privilege authorizes the INSERT.
changeSet.rollback: DROP FUNCTION IF EXISTS nexus_test.insert_chunk_bare_vector(text, text, bytea, int)

changeSet.author: nexus-3wh8d.13
changeSet.comment: RDR-225: nexus_test.insert_chunk_bare_vector supplies embedding_model once nexus.chunks has the column (vectors-030-1). The function is shared by two kinds of caller: the pre-walk dedicated containers (Hygiene002CollectionAttributesWalkTest, Hygiene004OwnerGrammarUnderscoreTest), where the column does not exist yet and the original three-column-key INSERT is the only valid one, and any caller on a fully walked cluster, where the row must carry its collection's model (a NOT NULL partition key, and the model partition's dimension CHECK). The function therefore asks information_schema which shape it is running against, at execution time, and takes the model from the collection's catalog_collections row; a collection with no row is refused by name instead of by the composite foreign key. Same signature, so the generated Routines.insertChunkBareVector is unchanged. SECURITY INVOKER.

changeSet.author: nexus-cbo4a
changeSet.comment: nexus_test.fts_matches(tsvector, text, text): SQL-language wrapper for p_vector @@ plainto_tsquery(p_config::regconfig, p_query) (nexus-cbo4a batch 13). jOOQ has no typed text-search operator; the three schema tests that probe a table's fts_vector (Plans, Memory, Scratch) call the generated Routines.ftsMatches Field instead of a condition("...") template. p_config is the regconfig name ('english' / 'simple'), cast inside the function so the Java side passes plain text. STABLE: plainto_tsquery with an explicit configuration does not read session state. SECURITY INVOKER.
changeSet.sql: CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION nexus_test.fts_matches(p_vector tsvector, p_config text, p_query text) RETURNS boolean LANGUAGE sql STABLE SECURITY INVOKER AS $$ SELECT p_vector @@ plainto_tsquery(p_config::regconfig, p_query) $$;
changeSet.rollback: DROP FUNCTION IF EXISTS nexus_test.fts_matches(tsvector, text, text)

changeSet.author: nexus-cbo4a
changeSet.comment: nexus_test.drop_index(regclass): plpgsql wrapper for DROP INDEX (nexus-cbo4a batch 13). jOOQ 3.20 never schema-qualifies an index name on POSTGRES (DropIndexImpl renders the index under qualify(false)), so DSLContext#dropIndex renders DROP INDEX "name" and resolves through the session search_path, which this project never relies on. p_index is regclass so PostgreSQL resolves the qualified identity with no string to validate; the body then renders the DROP from pg_class as an explicit %I.%I pair, never through regclassout, so the second resolution is by oid and not by search_path. SECURITY INVOKER so the caller's own privilege authorizes the DROP.

changeSet.author: nexus-3wh8d.8
changeSet.comment: nexus_test.p225_ts3_delete_and_reinsert(text, text, bytea): RDR-225 TS3 case (b) against the partitioned nexus.chunks (nexus-3wh8d.8). Under SET CONSTRAINTS nexus.fk_catalog_chunks_chunk DEFERRED it deletes one chunk row and re-inserts the same row in the same transaction; the deferred four-column manifest foreign key is checked at COMMIT and must pass. SET CONSTRAINTS has no jOOQ typed-DSL form, so it lives here (the test tree carries no raw SQL string). v_row is a RECORD, not nexus.chunks, because installTestObjects also runs at pre-walk migration points where that type may not exist yet. Called through the generated Routines on one autocommit statement, so the commit, and any foreign-key failure, is that statement's. SECURITY INVOKER: the caller's role and tenant GUC govern (nexus_svc under row-level security).
changeSet.rollback: DROP FUNCTION IF EXISTS nexus_test.p225_ts3_delete_and_reinsert(text, text, bytea)

changeSet.author: nexus-3wh8d.8
changeSet.comment: nexus_test.p225_ts3_delete_only(text, text, bytea): RDR-225 TS3 case (c) (nexus-3wh8d.8). Under SET CONSTRAINTS nexus.fk_catalog_chunks_chunk DEFERRED it deletes one chunk row and leaves any manifest row that names it; the deferred foreign key must fail the statement's own commit (SQLSTATE 23503). Same rationale and role as p225_ts3_delete_and_reinsert.
changeSet.rollback: DROP FUNCTION IF EXISTS nexus_test.p225_ts3_delete_only(text, text, bytea)

changeSet.author: nexus-3wh8d.8
changeSet.comment: nexus_test.p225_seed_random_chunks(text, text, text, int, int): RDR-225 (nexus-3wh8d.8) bulk seeder for the plan and lock measurements: p_n chunks with distinct chashes (sha256 of the index, so reruns collide only on purpose) and random unit-ish vectors of p_dim, filed under p_model, built server side so the test tree carries no vector literal strings. Inserts through the partitioned parent as the caller (superuser in the tests). The collection must already be registered under p_model.

changeSet.author: nexus-3wh8d.8
changeSet.comment: nexus_test.p225_explain_knn(text, text, int): RDR-225 (nexus-3wh8d.8) plan probe: the EXPLAIN (COSTS OFF) text of a nearest-neighbour query on the partitioned nexus.chunks with LITERAL tenant_id and embedding_model predicates (the shape the read path adds), so plan-time pruning applies. p_dim picks the vector column; the query vector is a constant built server side. Returns one text, lines joined by newlines. jOOQ's DSLContext#explain cannot express the pgvector distance operator without a plain-SQL template, so the probe lives here.
